entries.title: Everything the mod adds
q: what items does the mod add
what can i craft from this mod
how do i get mod items
entries.answer: Everything the mod adds has a real recipe, a use and a maker in town. Every recipe is in your recipe book; ask the Guide about any item by name.
more: Everything the mod adds is a real thing of real makings: a recipe, an age, a worth, a trade that makes it, and a use.

The groups: founding (kit, spawner, charter, board), shops (counter, sign, service counter, ribbon), coin, garments, dishes and drinks, field and work tools, home and play, quest items, honours, arms, the watch's and the Nether runners' kit, and your assistants' tools.
steps: Open your recipe book: every recipe is there from the start.
Creative: the Village Folk tab holds everything.
tips: The town's own makers make each thing when the town wants it; the shop's workshop makes things to your order.

entries.title: Things you can't craft, and how to get them
q: why is there no recipe for the deed
how do i get a deed
how do i get a working model
can i craft a memory core
entries.answer: Every block and item the mod adds is in your recipe book except five that are issued, not made: citizen papers, deeds, coins, memory cores and working models. A made one would be a forgery.
more: Citizen Papers: written at a Town Hall desk when you join a town (Town Hall → Join); a lost set is 2 coins to replace at the desk.
Deed: the register writes one for every title it holds, and hands it to you when you buy land or a house (Land, or Mortgages at the bank).
Village Coin: struck at the town's mint; bring gold ingots to a market stall's counter for eight coins each, or earn them by work and trade.
Memory Core: forms when a companion falls, holding all it was; nothing else makes one.
Working Model: the town's scholars build one each time they finish an invention; it goes to the stores and the museum.
Letters of demand from the bank or a court are notices in your planner and chat, not items.

Everything else, from the ballot box, business core, job board and whistle to the stocks, counters, troughs and crates, has a recipe that shows in the book from your first moment in the world. Three masters' recipes open when you finish an apprenticeship's second lesson.
steps: Open your recipe book: everything craftable is there.
For papers, join a town at its Town Hall.
For a deed, buy land or a house.
For coins, take gold ingots to a market stall's counter.
tips: The shop's workshop also makes any craftable thing to your order, out of the town's stores.

entries.title: Garments: coats, hats, scarves and brooches
entries.answer: The mod adds coats, jackets, shawls, waistcoats, hats, scarves, brooches and rosettes. Craft or buy one and give it to a folk to wear.
more: Garments a folk wears over its trade's clothes.

Long Coat (6 wool, a string), Leather Jacket (4 leather, a string), Wool Shawl (3 wool, 2 string), Waistcoat (5 wool, a gold nugget), Felt Hat (3 wool round a leather), Flat Cap (2 wool, a string), Top Hat (4 wool, a gold nugget), Wool Scarf (2 wool, a string), Brooch (2 gold nuggets, a lapis), Rosette (wool, paper, string: the fashion show's prize).
steps: Craft one, or buy it from the town's shop.
Dye it in a crafting grid with any dye, like leather armour (not the brooch).
Give it to a folk (Trade → Give) and it puts it on there and then.

entries.title: Banner patterns and the tabard
q: how do i put a banner on a tabard
entries.answer: Three new banner patterns (Fish, Pick and Sheaf) for the loom, and the Tabard, which takes a banner's arms at the crafting table.
tips: Folk wear their town's tabards on festival days and Founding Day.

entries.title: The towns' own dishes
entries.answer: Each town's land has its own dish with an effect, like Fish Stew (water breathing) or Cocoa Cake (haste). Eat them or find them on dining cards.
more: Each town's land has its dish, with an effect: Fish Stew (water breathing), Mushroom and Game Pie (night vision), Sweet Berry Tart (speed), Harvest Loaf (regeneration), Miner's Hotpot (resistance), Spiced Mutton (fire resistance), Cocoa Cake (haste), Fen Broth (night vision).
tips: Recipes: fish stew (bowl, cod or salmon, baked potato, carrot); game pie (2 wheat, brown and red mushroom, egg, roast rabbit/pork/chicken); berry tart (3 berries, 2 wheat, sugar, egg); harvest loaf (3 wheat, egg, seeds); hotpot (bowl, roast mutton, 2 baked potatoes); spiced mutton (roast mutton, beetroot, sugar); cocoa cake (2 cocoa, 2 wheat, sugar, egg); fen broth (bowl, two mushrooms, beetroot).
The town's dish is marked 'local' on a dining card.

entries.title: The kitchen and cellar: cheese, cakes, mead, cider
entries.answer: The kitchen adds packed lunches, cheese, honey cake, mead, cider and fish pie, each with a real recipe.
more: Packed Lunch (bread, cooked meat or fish and an apple, makes 2), Cheese Wheel (3 milk buckets, 3 wheat, an egg; cut into 4 Slices of Cheese), Honey Cake (honey bottle, 2 wheat, egg, sugar; for birthdays, weddings and festivals), Mead (honey bottle, sugar, glass bottle), Cider (3 apples, sugar, glass bottle) and Fish Pie (cod or salmon, potato, wheat, egg).
tips: The cheese wheel is a block: set it out on a table.

entries.title: The masters' recipes: reinforced pickaxe, stout, pie
q: why cant i craft the reinforced pickaxe
entries.answer: Three recipes only a taught player can craft: the Reinforced Pickaxe, Brewer's Stout and Farmhouse Pie. Learn them as a master's apprentice.
more: Three recipes only a taught player can craft: the Reinforced Pickaxe (an iron pickaxe, three iron and a copper strap: three times the wear), the Brewer's Stout (two wheat, sugar and a bottle: Haste for two minutes, the bottle comes back) and the Farmhouse Pie (three wheat, a pumpkin, an egg and a carrot, makes 2: ten hunger).
warn: Before the lesson the crafting grid gives you nothing; after it, the recipe is in your book.

entries.title: Tools of the fields and pens
q: how do i use the watering can
entries.answer: Tools for the fields and pens: watering can, seed satchel, sickle, nesting box, feed trough, fish trap, rain barrel and bee smoker.
more: Copper Watering Can (5 copper: 16 waterings, each soaks a 3×3 and grows crops a little), Seed Satchel (string over 2 leather: 4 stacks of seed), Copper Sickle (3 copper on a stick: reaps a ripe crop and the eight round it), Nesting Box (5 planks round a wheat: hens lay in it), Feed Trough (4 planks round a slab: herds eat and breed off it), Fish Trap (6 sticks, 2 string round a bait: catches fish by itself), Rain Barrel (7 planks round a copper: four buckets of rain), Bee Smoker (2 copper, a leather and a coal: hives emptied without stings).
tips: Fill the watering can at a rain barrel or water.

entries.title: Tools of the mine, woods and roads
q: chest you can pick up full
entries.answer: Tools for the mine, woods and roads: pit props, rope, ore sack, felling saw, thatch, milestones, shipping crates and window boxes.
more: Pit Prop (3 planks over 2 logs, makes 4: holds up gravel and sand), Rope Coil (4 string round a leather: let it down any drop and climb it; break it to take it up), Ore Sack (3 leather, 2 string: 4 stacks of ore), Felling Saw (2 iron, 2 sticks, a string: sneak as you cut a log and the whole tree comes down), Thatch (6 wheat makes 4; stairs and slabs), Milestone (5 cobblestone round a sign: lettered with towns and distances), Shipping Crate (6 planks, 2 logs, an iron nugget: a chest you can pick up full), Window Box (3 planks, earth and a flower: hang under a window).

entries.title: Home comforts: quilts and paper lanterns
q: how do i make a quilt
entries.answer: The Patchwork Quilt makes a better night's sleep; Paper Lanterns (sixteen colours) light the square at festivals.
more: The Patchwork Quilt (six wool in two rows of three, of three colours or more) is laid over a bed: a better night, warm in winter.

entries.title: Medal and Key of the Town
q: what does the town medal do
entries.answer: The Medal and the Key of the Town are honours for your quests; carry them and folk warm to you faster and the stores sell cheaper.
more: The Medal of the Town is struck for you when you finish a quest story there; the Key to the Town comes after two stories or ten quests once the town counts you a friend (with a feast and the title Freeman).
tips: A town short of gold votes you the honour and owes it until the gold comes in.

entries.title: Gold Charm and Runner's Satchel
entries.answer: The Gold Charm keeps piglins calm; the Runner's Satchel carries nine stacks and floats in lava.
more: The Gold Charm (a string over a gold ingot between gold nuggets) is worn on the head: piglins leave you be as with gold armour, a point of armour, and it never wears out.

entries.title: Spectacles
entries.answer: Give Spectacles to an old folk who has none: it puts them on at once and is delighted.
more: Spectacles (3 gold nuggets and 2 glass panes): hand them to an old folk who has none and it puts them on there and then, delighted (a big boost to how it feels about you).

entries.title: War Horn
q: how do i use the war horn
entries.answer: The War Horn sounds army calls: sneak and use to pick a call, use to sound it.
more: Made from a goat horn and a leather, or two bones, a copper ingot and a leather.
Sneak-use picks the call (muster, march, form up, begin, charge, rally, retreat, victory); use sounds it.
If you lead the town or fight in its army, its army in the field answers.

entries.title: Fishing Net
q: how do i use the fishing net
entries.answer: Cast a Fishing Net over open water for two to four fish a haul. Five string make one.
more: Cast it over open water, from a boat or off the bank: it comes up with two to four fish a haul, with a while between casts and a little wear each time.

entries.title: Driving Whip
entries.answer: The Driving Whip is a carter's whip for driving wagons between towns.
more: The carter's whip, carried on a wagon's bench (a stick, string and leather).
Towns' carters drive wagons on the roads between towns; ask one 'The wagon's road' to hear where it's bound.

entries.title: Stocks
entries.answer: Stocks are where a convicted folk sits out its sentence on the square.
more: Set a pair on a town's square and they're the town's the first time it wants them.
